name: Distance Tree (easy version)
description: This version of the problem differs from the next one only in the constraint on $$$n$$$ . A tree is a connected undirected graph without cycles. A weighted tree has a weight assigned to each edge. The distance between two vertices is the minimum sum of weights on the path connecting them. You are given a weighted tree with $$$n$$$ vertices, each edge has a weight of $$$1$$$. Denote $$$d(v)$$$ as the distance between vertex $$$1$$$ and vertex $$$v$$$. Let $$$f(x)$$$ be the minimum possible value of $$$\max\limits_{1 \leq v \leq n} \ {d(v)}$$$ if you can temporarily add an edge with weight $$$x$$$ between any two vertices $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ $$$(1 \le a, b \le n)$$$. Note that after this operation, the graph is no longer a tree. For each integer $$$x$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, find $$$f(x)$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 3000$$$). Each of the next $$$n−1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u,v \le n$$$) indicating that there is an edge between vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$3000$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print $$$n$$$ integers in a single line, $$$x$$$-th of which is equal to $$$f(x)$$$ for all $$$x$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1632E1 — Distance Tree (easy version) [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
